title: Amanirenas, kandake of Kush
summary: Amanirenas was a kandake (queen) of Kush in the late first century BCE. Around 25 BCE her forces took Aswan, Elephantine and Philae from Roman Egypt. Rome's governor Petronius pushed south, and Kush negotiated with Augustus on Samos, gaining concessions including a Roman withdrawal to the north. Strabo is the main source, and details are disputed.

uncertainty.note: History.com gives the campaign as "From 25 to 21 B.C."; WorldAtlas dates the invasion to 25 or 24 BCE and the Samos treaty to 21 or 20 BCE. Her birth and death are not given.

where.modern_name: Meroe, River Nile State, Sudan (pin is Meroe, where a bronze head of Augustus was found and from which one source says she ruled)
where.historical_name: Meroe, a royal centre of the Kingdom of Kush; the opened sources differ on whether Napata or Meroe was her residence

importance.justification: Kushite queen who led a war with Roman Egypt that ended in a treaty described as favourable to Kush.

sources.title: The Nubian Queen Who Fought Back Caesar's Army
The One-Eyed African Queen Who Defeated the Great Roman Empire

reviewer_note: The two opened pages disagree on whether Petronius sacked Napata, on her residence (Napata vs Meroe) and on treaty terms; those points are left out or hedged. Only popular pages were opened; a scholarly source is needed for the full record.
